My values for the schools are w = $73, x = $60, y = $43, z = $60. My priority rankings at the schools are w: 1, x: 2, y: 1, z: 2. Most applicants favor y > x > w > z.

My next best value is x and z, both at $60. I am the second priority at both x and z. If rejected from w, I will propose to x. If rejected from x, I will propose to z.

Since x and z have the same value to me, and I am a second priority at both, the key is which school is likely to have more applicants *ahead* of me. Given the general applicant preference for y > x > w > z, x is likely to be more competitive than z. Therefore, if rejected from w and x, I have a better chance of getting into z.

Therefore, I will rank w first, then x, then z, and lastly y. While y has a higher applicant preference, its value to me is significantly lower than w, x, or z. I'm banking on my high ranking at w and a reasonable chance at x or z.
